item.title: Finite zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols
item.description: arXiv:2610.30209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.
item.dc:creator: Youqi Liu, Jie Qin, Sui Huang

item.title: Fefferman--Chang-type atomic decompositions for product Hardy spaces associated with Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.30459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a geometric (Fefferman--Chang-type) atomic characterization of the two-parameter Hardy space associated with a pair of Schr\"odinger operators $L_i=-\Delta+V_i$ on $\mathbb R^{n_i}$, $i=1,2$. The space is defined by the product conical square function. We assume comparability of neighbouring covering cubes, a local bound on the potentials, and decay of the semigroup mass at large scales. We prove that the Hardy norm is equivalent to a sum of classical local product Hardy norms at scales determined by the adapted coverings. This localization formula yields an atomic decomposition whose atoms satisfy size and partial cancellation conditions, with cancellation required only below the corresponding local scales. Both the atoms and their rectangular components remain supported inside fixed enlargements of the covering rectangles. The proof combines one-parameter Schr\"odinger Hardy space characterizations with standard vector-valued arguments and a localized product atomic decomposition with uniform control of scales and supports. The assumptions cover the model case of reverse H\"older potentials $V\in RH_q$, $q>n/2$, as well as potentials outside every $RH_q$ class, $q>1$, including half-space indicators and exponential potentials.
item.dc:creator: Agnieszka Hejna-{\L}y\.zwa

item.title: Matrix Triangle Inequalities: Past, Present, and Future
item.description: arXiv:2610.30538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This survey provides a concise overview of matrix triangle inequalities. Classical topics, such as inequalities for unitarily invariant norms, are revisited from a different perspective, with a particular emphasis on unitary orbit inequalities and various notions of matrix moduli. The exposition progresses from elementary results to much more recent developments, highlighting the evolution of the subject and its ongoing directions of research.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Christophe Bourin, Teng Zhang

item.title: Very tight embeddings of subspaces of \(L_p\) for \(0<p<1\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.30546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For \(0<p<1\) and \(\mu>1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloor\mu d\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,\mu)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p<q\leq2\), the distortion is at most \(C(p,q,\mu)T\), independently of \(d\). We also give explicit bounds as \(\mu\downarrow1\). This answers the question of Johnson and Schechtman concerning the extension of their very tight embedding theorem below exponent one. The proof combines compression at a lower exponent with a change of density that preserves the number of coordinates, and applies over both scalar fields.
item.dc:creator: Gang Cai, Longfa Sun

item.title: Schatten limits for semi-commutators in Toeplitz quantization on Fock space
item.description: arXiv:2610.30787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve a problem posed by Hu and Virtanen by characterizing, for every $0<p<\infty$, the bounded symbols $f$ for which $T_f^{(t)}T_g^{(t)}-T_{fg}^{(t)}$ tends to zero in the unnormalized Schatten $p$-norm or quasi-norm as $t\to0^+$ for every fixed bounded $g$. The setting is weighted Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^n$ with weights whose real Hessians are uniformly positive and bounded. Only constants satisfy the limit when $p<2n$; at $p=2n$, it is equivalent to the weak real gradient belonging to $L^{2n}(\mathbb R^{2n})$. When $p>2n$, the limit is characterized by relative weak compactness in $L^1(\mathbb R^{2n})$ of normalized local mean oscillation densities. For $p\ge2$, uniform convergence over $\|g\|_\infty\le1$ is equivalent to vanishing density mass. A continuous compactly supported counterexample for $p>2n$ shows that bounded density mass and convergence for $g=\bar f$ do not imply convergence for every fixed bounded $g$. The symbol classes are weight-independent unital algebras, yielding limits for finite Toeplitz products and commutators; quantitative H\"older estimates also give finite-rank approximation bounds. The Gaussian case transfers to anti-Wick quantization by unitary equivalence. On compact K\"ahler manifolds with positive line bundles, we prove a H\"older sufficient condition, including the endpoint, for each fixed bounded second symbol. A projective-line example shows that trace norm convergence can fail for a smooth first symbol and a fixed bounded second symbol. The proofs combine local holomorphic approximation, Schatten and Sobolev estimates, singular integral methods, and the Dunford--Pettis criterion.
item.dc:creator: Jie Qin

item.title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and quantitative Fourier--Schur separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ordinary and completely bounded norms of radial Schur multipliers on trees. On the homogeneous tree of countably infinite degree, we show that boundedness implies complete boundedness. The argument realizes arbitrary matrix amplifications of a shifted Toeplitz symbol inside rectangular corners of the original multiplier. It also applies to some locally finite trees of unbounded degree. Consequently, the completely bounded radial multiplier theorem of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet, P\'erez Garc\'ia and Wang has no general counterpart with ordinary norms. We also determine the optimal order of the comparison constant for positive definite even symbols. For each $1 < p < \infty$ with $p \neq 2$, we construct radial symbols on finitely generated nonabelian free groups, supported in the ball of radius $N$, whose completely bounded Herz--Schur norms remain bounded as $N \to \infty$, whereas their ordinary Fourier multiplier norms grow at least like $N^{|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$. For each fixed $0 < \vartheta < \pi$, we also determine the exact order $t^{-|1-\frac{2}{p}|}$ of both the ordinary and completely bounded Fourier multiplier norms of the damped radial phases $s \mapsto \mathrm{e}^{(-t+\mathrm{i}\vartheta)|s|}$ as $t \to 0$. Finally, we compute the local amenability modulus of free balls, we bound the Fourier--Schur ratio of free balls from above and below in terms of this modulus, and we show that its restriction to radial symbols grows polynomially in the radius.
item.dc:creator: C\'edric Arhancet

item.title: Optimal weighted sampling of positive and normal operator orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.31278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted sampling of operator orbit frames in infinite dimensional separable Hilbert spaces \(H\), keeping the operator and generating vectors fixed. Let $N_\mu(R)$ count the sampling times in $[0,R]$. For a single orbit of a positive operator, let $m_A(R)$ count the eigenvalues in $(0,e^{-1/R}]$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property must satisfy the lower bound $N_\mu(R)\ge m_A(R)-O_\mu(1)$. Conversely, for every $\eta>0$, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_\mu(R)\le(1+\eta)m_A(R)+O_\eta(1)$. Thus the coefficient $1$ is optimal. Under additional spectral conditions, we attain $N_\mu(R)=m_A(R)+O(1)$ and characterize the weights that preserve the frame property on the constructed sets. For finitely or countably many orbits of a positive operator, let $P_j$, $j\ge1$, be the spectral projection corresponding to $2^{-j-1}<-\log\lambda\le2^{-j}$ and define $K_A(R)=\#\{j\ge1:2^j\le R,\ P_j\ne0\}$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property satisfies $N_\mu(R)\ge c_\mu K_A(R)-C_\mu$ for $R\ge2$, with constants $c_\mu>0$ and $C_\mu\ge0$. Conversely, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_\mu(R)\le L K_A(R)+L$ for $R\ge2$, where $L$ depends only on the bounds of the given orbit frame. For normal operators of norm one, we prove that the smallest frame condition number is attained among integer sampling designs that preserve the frame property and satisfy a prescribed counting bound, whenever this class is nonempty. Finally, we construct one normal operator with two families of generating vectors for which the optimal growth orders of $N_\mu(R)$ are $\log R$ and $R$, respectively, for both real and integer sampling.
item.dc:creator: Jian Wu

item.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.31382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: A sphere obstruction for the Hilbert shift quotient
item.description: arXiv:2610.31468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and let $\mathbb Z$ act by bilateral shifts. We prove that the quotient $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ of the unit sphere, equipped with its quotient metric, has infinite Hilbert distortion. Consequently, $\mathcal H/\mathbb Z$ does not admit a bilipschitz embedding into Hilbert space, answering a question of Cahill, Iverson, and Mixon. The proof first embeds every flat torus $\mathbb R^n/L$, after rescaling, into the quotient $\mathbb S\big(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n)\big)/\mathbb Z^n$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$, where $\mathbb Z^n$ acts by translations. We then show that every finite subset of this quotient embeds into $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$. The lower bounds of Khot and Naor for the Hilbert distortion of flat tori then imply the result.
item.dc:creator: Avik Das, Christian Rosendal

item.title: Searching for the power rangers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. We identify a condition which enables us to show that the range of each power map is comeager; a strengthening of this condition allows us to prove that a generic element embeds in a flow (a continuous, one-parameter subgroup). This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Carroy, Julien Melleray

item.title: Relaxation and $\Gamma$-Convergence of Stretch Energy on Surface Homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.30214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $\Gamma$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Yung Liu

item.title: Computable presentations of separable Lebesgue spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.30565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every right-c.e.\ real $p\in(1,2)$, $L^p[0,1]$ has a computable presentation. The proof combines an effective stability modulus for almost isometric embeddings with a Fra\"{\i}ss\'e-style construction in which the exponent varies. In the same range, if $\ell^p$ has a computable presentation, then $p$ is computable. Combining these with the known results gives the computable presentability classification for all separable Lebesgue spaces. We also formulate an effective Fra\"{\i}ss\'e theorem for Banach spaces and apply it to obtain a computable presentation of the Gurarij Banach space.
item.dc:creator: Ruofei Xie, Xuanheng Zhao

item.title: When are metrizable linear subspaces of topological vector spaces finite-dimensional?
item.description: arXiv:2610.30800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study conditions that imply finite-dimensionality of metrizable or Frechet-Urysohn linear subspaces of topological vector spaces (TVS). We consider the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ of TVS: a space $L$ belongs to $\mathscr{D}_M$ (respectively, $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$) if every metrizable (respectively, Frechet-Urysohn) linear subspace of $L$ is finite-dimensional. Although the classes of metrizable spaces and of Frechet-Urysohn spaces differ substantially, the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ are much closer to each other: in the Hrusak-Ramos-Garcia model, in which Malykhin's problem is solved, $\mathscr{D}_M=\mathscr{D}_{FU}$, whereas under MA+not CH, as shown in the paper, $\mathscr{D}_M\neq\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. For a locally convex space (LCS) $L$ we denote by $L_w$ the space $L$ with its weak topology and by $L'_{w^*}$ the dual space with the weak$^*$ topology. This paper investigates which LCS $L$ have the property that $L_w$ and $L'_{w^*}$ belong to $\mathscr{D}_M$ or $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. Although the classes are close, different methods are used to study them: topological-algebraic ones for $\mathscr{D}_M$ (a criterion is obtained) and methods of measure theory and probability for $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ (a sufficient condition is obtained). We prove that if an LCS $L$ admits a continuous norm, then $L_w\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; in particular, if $L$ admits a continuous norm and $L_w$ is Frechet-Urysohn, then $L$ is finite-dimensional. If the topology of an LCS $L$ is coarser than the topology induced by some complete norm on $L$ (for example, if $L$ is Banach), then $L'_{w^*}\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; completeness of the norm is essential here. The methods also apply to spaces of real-analytic functions and to the space of polynomials with the topology of pointwise convergence: these also belong to $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav V. Maksimov, Evgenii A. Reznichenko

item.title: Dual medial axes in finite-dimensional normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.30878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study medial axes of nonempty closed sets in finite-dimensional real normed spaces whose norms are $C^1$ away from the origin. Using the differential of the norm, we define the dual $k$-medial axis by requiring the contact covectors associated with nearest points to have affine dimension at least $k-1$. In dimension $n$, we prove that this set is $(n-k+1)$-rectifiable for every $1\le k\le n+1$, and hence has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-k+1$. We give a direct geometric proof and characterize the dual medial axes through the superdifferential of the squared distance function, obtaining an alternative proof from a theorem of Alberti, Ambrosio, and Cannarsa on singularities of semiconvex functions. Under the additional assumption of strict convexity, the ordinary and dual medial axes coincide for $k=2,3$, yielding the corresponding rectifiability results for ordinary medial axes. For $k=4$, however, the ordinary rectifiability conclusion can fail even for norms arbitrarily close to Euclidean: we construct norms on $\mathbb R^3$ with smooth positively curved unit spheres arbitrarily $C^\infty$-close to the Euclidean sphere, together with four-point sets whose ordinary $4$-medial axes contain nondegenerate line segments.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Durand, Xiangyu Liang, Sicheng Zhang

item.title: Safety-constrained position tracking of a flexible transmission system
item.description: arXiv:2610.31061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider safety-constrained position tracking for a flexible transmission system consisting of a torsional shaft driven by a motor and connected to a gravitationally loaded inertia. The coupled PDE-ODE dynamics admit a semilinear formulation in which the linear input-output system is impedance passive and the gravitational torque enters as a bounded, globally Lipschitz perturbation. We establish an energy dissipation inequality for the nonlinear model and show that a position-funnel controller with supervised damping admits a unique global closed-loop trajectory. In particular, the motor-angle tracking error remains strictly inside a prescribed time-varying funnel, which can be chosen to enforce safety bounds on the motor angle.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hastir, Timo Reis

item.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.31174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.
item.dc:creator: Denghui Luo, Geng Tian

item.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
item.description: arXiv:2610.31255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fr\'echet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
item.dc:creator: El-Mahdi Nafia, Aziz El Ghazouani, M'hamed El Omari

item.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < \pi/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $\pi/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Larotonda

item.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L\log L$ endpoint
item.description: arXiv:2610.31560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L\log L$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. This answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006}.
item.dc:creator: Hiranmoy Ghorui, Suman Mondal, Samya Kumar Ray

item.title: Mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and their applications to boundedness of operators
item.description: arXiv:2603.15353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and obtain their preduals. The boundedness of Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, iterated maximal operator, fractional integral operator, singular integral operator on these spaces is proved. In addition, we give a description of the dual of mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and conclude the reflexivity of these spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Bai, Pengfei Guo, Jingshi Xu

item.title: The stability landscape in wave-packet scattering: geometric rigidity and sharp Sobolev thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2607.21578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central problem in harmonic analysis is to understand how frequency resolution constrains stability under nonlinear changes of coordinates. Motivated by Mallat's wavelet scattering theory, we establish a sharp resolution--robustness principle for nonlinear representations built from two-dimensional wave-packet systems, showing that the transverse geometry of the frequency channels determines the critical Sobolev regularity. Whenever the channels are thinner than in the wavelet regime, arbitrarily small smooth deformations can move high-frequency mass between adjacent channels, producing instability already at the level of the linear filter bank and the first scattering layer. We match this obstruction with scale-sharp commutator estimates propagated through the full scattering cascade, obtaining Lipschitz stability at the critical regularity threshold. Together, the results provide the first intrinsic deformation-stability theory for non-wavelet Euclidean scattering transforms and identify a microlocal transport mechanism governing robustness across nonlinear multiscale representations.
item.dc:creator: Max Getter, S. Ivan Trapasso

item.title: Unbounded Helson Forms with a Moment Representation
item.description: arXiv:2610.12252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the positive Helson form $h_0[a,b]=\sum_{m,n\ge1}\alpha(mn)a_n\overline{b_m}$ on the finitely supported sequences $c_{00}\subset\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$, where $\alpha(n)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}n^{-s}d\mu(s)<\infty$ for a finite positive Borel measure $\mu$. Under the Carleman condition $\sum_{k\ge1}\alpha(4^k)^{-1/(2k)}=\infty$, closability of $h_0$ is equivalent to $\sqrt{n}\alpha(n)\to0$, and hence to $\mu((-\infty,1/2])=0$. For measures concentrated on $(1/2,\infty)$, we identify the closure of the operator $N_0a=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}$, defined on $c_{00}$, with its maximal realization from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$ to $L^2(\mu)$. We further prove that the sequences $a\in c_{00}$ satisfying $\sum_{n\ge1}a_n/\sqrt{n}=0$ form an operator core for the positive self-adjoint operator associated with the closure of $h_0$.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Ma, Yufeng Lu, Chao Zu

item.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.22185v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-\v{S}mulian theorems.
item.dc:creator: Tiexin Guo, Xiaohuan Mu, Pasqualetto Enrico, Qiang Tu, Guang Yang

item.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24821v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang, Jimmie Lawson

item.title: Persistence of gaps in the spectrum of certain almost periodic operators
item.description: arXiv:math/0504088v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that for any irrational rotation number and any admissible gap labelling number the almost Mathieu operator (also known as Harper's operator) has a gap in its spectrum with that labelling number. This answers the strong version of the so-called "Ten Martini Problem". When specialized to the particular case where the coupling constant is equal to one, it follows that the "Hofstadter butterfly" has for any quantum Hall conductance the exact number of components prescribed by the recursive scheme to build this fractal structure.
item.dc:creator: Norbert Riedel

item.title: On isoperimetric local-Bollob\'as-Thomason inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2601.15044v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the following isoperimetric-type inequality: for every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and some $\sigma\subset[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there exists a suitable Hanner polytope $B_K$ with the same volume as $K$ and such that the volume of each of its orthogonal projections onto every subspace whose basis is formed by the canonical vectors $\{e_i:i\in\tau\cup([n]\setminus\sigma)\}$, for every $\tau\subseteq\sigma$, bounds from below the volume of the corresponding projections of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno

item.title: Geometric Properties of Higher Dimensional Solenoidal Attractors
item.dc:creator: Daniele Galli, Eleonora Passaglia, Andrea Ulliana

item.title: On the Geometry of Wasserstein Barycenter II: Riemannian Rigidity, Essential Non-Branching, and Finsler Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.19564v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wasserstein barycenters provide a notion of weighted mean for probability measures on a metric space. We prove that the barycenter curvature-dimension condition ${\rm BCD}(K,N)$ is equivalent to ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ for $K\in \mathbb R$ and $1<N<\infty$. This gives a new characterization of Riemannian curvature-dimension spaces by entropy inequalities at barycenters of finite families of measures. As a byproduct, we introduce an almost ${\rm BCD}$ condition that allows an additive error in the entropy inequality. It is stable under measured Gromov-Hausdorff convergence and implies essential non-branching when the error is sufficiently small. The resulting class contains non-Riemannian Finsler spaces. Within the ${\rm BCD}$ framework, this answers an open problem posed by Ambrosio in his 2018 ICM survey. We further bound the failure of the parallelogram identity for cotangent norms in terms of the entropy error.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Deng-Yu Liu
